newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian Senate approves key telecom bill.
newsitem.headline: Italian Senate approves key telecom bill.

text.p: Italy's upper house of parliament (Senate) on Tuesday gave the final go-ahead to a government bill, paving the way for the privatisation of state telecoms group Telecom Italia.

The bill, which was approved earlier this month by the lower house of parliament and now becomes law, creates a telecoms sector regulatory watchdog which is a prerequisite to the long-awaited sale of Telecom Italia.
Tuesday's vote was approved by a show of hands, with government backers grouped in the centre-left Olive Tree coalition supporting the bill and centre-right opposition parties abstaining.

The bill has spent years crawling through parliament, with opponents to the privatisation process, especially the hardleft Communist Refoundation, using the draft law as an opportunity to delay the sale of Telecom Italia.
But Prime Minister Romano Prodi has finally convinced Refoundation to back the project and the Telecom Italia sell-off, dubbed the mother of all privatisations, is now planned for October.

"I'm very satisfied," Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico told reporters. "We have approved a very important bill which is in line with European Union directives and puts Italy in the forefront of the European telecoms sector."
